articles.title: Canada has important information for international students: Starting September 1, we are changing the …
articles.summary: Tech News News: Canada has introduced higher financial requirements for international students applying for study permits starting today (September 1). According to t.
articles.body: Canada has introduced higher financial requirements for international students applying for study permits starting today (September 1). According to the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, applicants must now show increased proof of funds to demonstrate their ability to support themselves during their studies. The change is aimed at reflecting rising living costs and ensuring that students are financially prepared. This new requirement put forward by IRCC sets the cost-of-living proof at 75% of Statistics Canada’s Low Income Cut-Off (LICO), in addition to tuition and travel expenses. "Important information for international students: starting September 1, 2026, the amount of funds you will need to demonstrate when applying for a study permit will increase. We update the financial resource requirements applicable to study permit applicants each year to adjust them to the cost of living and to help protect international students from any exploitation," wrote IRCC in a post shared on X (formerly knonw as Twitter).For a single applicant outside Quebec, the minimum proof of funds has risen to CAD $23,448, an increase of $553 over the previous threshold. The amounts scale higher depending on family size, with applicants required to show additional funds for each dependent.In Quebec, students must meet separate financial thresholds tied to the Quebec Acceptance Certificate (QAC). As of January 1, 2026, a single applicant must show CAD $24,617, with higher requirements for families.Canada student visa: Who's affected and by how muchThe increase applies to applicants intending to study anywhere in Canada outside Quebec, which has its own separate requirements. A single applicant with no dependants will need to show $553 more than under the previous threshold. Larger families face steeper jumps — an applicant bringing six additional family members will need $1,465 more than before.These cost-of-living figures are added on top of whatever amount is already required to cover the first full year of tuition and travel to and from Canada, meaning the total financial bar for approval is rising across the board, not just the cost-of-living component in isolation.The new dollar amountsAccording to the immigration department's updated guidance, published August 28, 2026, the new required amounts by family size are as follows:•1 applicant (principal only): $23,448 (up $553)•2 family members: $29,192 (up $690)•3 family members: $35,888 (up $848)•4 family members: $43,572 (up $1,029)•5 family members: $49,419 (up $1,167)•6 family members: $55,736 (up $1,316)•7 family members: $62,054 (up $1,465)•Each additional family member beyond seven: $6,318 (up $148)Applications submitted before September 1, 2026 will still be assessed under the previous cost-of-living amounts that were in effect at the time they were received. Applicants whose study programs run longer than one year must also explain how they intend to fund the remainder of their studies beyond that first year.Family MembersAmount Required (Sept 1 onward)Increase1 (principal applicant)CAD $23,448+$5532CAD $29,192+$6903CAD $35,888+$8484CAD $43,572+$1,0295CAD $49,419+$1,1676CAD $55,736+$1,3167CAD $62,054+$1,465Each additional memberCAD $6,318+$148What counts as acceptable proof of fundsIRCC accepts documentation across three broad categories. The first covers fees already paid, such as a receipt showing tuition and housing costs have been settled — though this must still be paired with separate evidence of funds available for living and travel expenses.The second category covers funds currently available, which can include proof of a student or education loan from a bank, a Canadian bank account in the student's name showing transferred funds, a guaranteed investment certificate from a Canadian bank, bank statements from the past six months (Canadian or foreign), pension plan documentation, or proof of rental income.The third category covers expected or promised support, including proof of a scholarship or a Government of Canada-funded education program, recent pay stubs, or a letter from a financial supporter. That letter must confirm the supporter's relationship to the applicant, their occupation, any dependants they have, and the specific amount of support they intend to provide — along with supporting evidence verifying the applicant's connection to that person and a copy of the supporter's identification or business registration.IRCC notes these examples aren't exhaustive, and applicants may need to provide additional documentation depending on their country and individual circumstances. Applicants from countries with foreign exchange controls must also show they'll be permitted to export the necessary funds to Canada.Separate, higher requirements for QuebecStudents planning to study in Quebec face a different process entirely. They must first obtain a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (QAC) before applying to IRCC for a study permit, and must meet Quebec-specific living expense requirements that are notably higher than the federal amounts. Those figures, last updated January 1, 2026, range from $24,617 for a single applicant up to $60,299 for six family members, with each additional family member requiring $5,254 — figures that, notably, don't include tuition or transportation costs.Both the Quebec provincial government and the federal government assess an applicant's proof of financial support, but they evaluate the same pool of funds — applicants aren't required to show separate or additional funds for the federal IRCC assessment on top of what they've already demonstrated to Quebec.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Family travels to Nepal to search for Bartlett woman missing in flood aftermath: 'Not losing hope'
articles.summary: ABC7 spoke with one of Poonam Thakkar's friends, who was supposed to be on the trip to Nepal and is now part of the effort in North America to help find her.
articles.body:
The family of a Bartlett woman missing after deadly flooding in Nepal has taken its search directly to the disaster zone, with one of her sisters arriving in Kathmandu to look for answers.

Gunjan Thakkar said her 42-year-old sister, Poonam Thakkar, traveled to the region as part of a Hindu pilgrimage near Mount Kailash. The family says they lost contact with her following the flooding and landslides and that she has since been officially declared missing.

According to the family, another of Thakkar's sisters arrived in Nepal on Monday and immediately began searching.

Before communication stopped, Thakkar sent what her longtime friend, Somali Raturi, described as one of her last video messages from Nepal.

In the video, Thakkar says, "Hello everyone, I am on the way to the border of Nepal and China."

Raturi said the last time she spoke with Thakkar was one day before the disaster.

"The last time we spoke was the day before the natural disaster on 25th of August," Raturi said.

Raturi said Thakkar shared videos from the trip, including scenes of the landscape she was visiting.

"She showed the place over a video, and a beautiful river running through the gorge, valleys," Raturi said.

The trip to Mount Kailash was years in the making.

"We were making plans for this spiritual pilgrimage for over two years, together with one of my other friends," Raturi said.

"It was our childhood, sort of, bucket list dream to be there," she said.

Raturi had planned to make the journey herself but said an injury forced her to cancel. She is now helping search for information from North America while Thakkar's family searches in Nepal.

According to Raturi, Thakkar's relatives wasted no time after arriving in the country.

"As soon as they landed, they left their bags in the hotel and then they went marching one place to another," she said.

The family says updates from government officials have been limited since Thakkar disappeared, leaving loved ones waiting for information.

Despite the uncertainty, family and friends say they have not given up hope.

"We are not losing hope. That's why the families get on the ground to find her and bring her back. And we have our hopes high that no news is great news. We will find something, and we will find them," Raturi said.

Raturi said someone answered when loved ones called Thakkar's Nepali phone a day after the flooding. However, because of a language barrier, they were unable to determine whether that person had any information about her.

The family says it is continuing to search for answers while asking for positive thoughts and prayers as efforts to locate Thakkar continue.

articles.title: In 1998, Steve Jobs convinced a 37-year-old Tim Cook to join near-bankrupt Apple, here's the 'story' he told to make him leave world's biggest PC company
articles.summary: Tech News News: Tim Cook concluded his 15-year tenure as Apple’s CEO on August 31, 2026, transitioning to executive chairman of the board effective September 1, 2026..
articles.body: Tim Cook concluded his 15-year tenure as Apple’s CEO on August 31, 2026, transitioning to executive chairman of the board effective September 1, 2026. John Ternus, formerly senior vice president of hardware engineering, has officially taken the helm of the company. While Cook leaves behind an era defined by monumental commercial success, his beginnings at the company were far more modest. Back in early 1998, Apple was on the edge of financial collapse, struggling with plunging staff morale, and widely viewed as an undesirable employer across Silicon Valley. Yet, Steve Jobs managed to convince a 37-year-old rising executive to walk away from Compaq, which was then the global leader in personal computer sales, and join the struggling company.Before making the leap, Cook had built an extensive corporate resume, spending 12 years at IBM alongside key executive roles at Intelligent Electronics and Compaq. While Cook had repeatedly rejected outreach from Apple's recruitment team, he eventually agreed to a face-to-face sit-down with Jobs. Cook later explained to Charlie Rose in 2014 that he felt compelled to meet the person who had essentially built the modern computing industry and was pursuing a distinctive vision.Steve Jobs’ vision of the iMac G3During their introductory discussion, Jobs reportedly laid out his roadmap to revitalise Apple, describing an upcoming computer concept designed to upend the entire PC landscape. CNBC reported that Jobs shared preliminary details of a hardware design unlike anything on the market. The concept later materialised as the iMac G3, the vibrant, translucent computer that turned designer Jony Ive into an industry star.Cook walked away from the encounter fascinated by the design and convinced that collaborating alongside Jobs would represent the privilege of a lifetime.Tim Cook ignored ‘career advice’ from peersTaking the role required Cook to defy the advice of his closest peers and all conventional logic. Reflecting on the decision during his 2010 Auburn University commencement address, Cook noted that any logical cost-benefit evaluation favoured staying at Compaq. One chief executive even warned Cook that leaving the market leader for Apple would be foolish.Cook believed that following the crowd was a mistake. Recognizing the deep operational challenges facing Apple, he decided he could make a meaningful impact and trusted his intuition over traditional career calculations.Apple hired Tim Cook in March 1998In March 1998, Jobs formally appointed Cook as senior vice president of worldwide operations, providing him a base compensation of $400,000 alongside a $500,000 signing bonus. Cook took charge of completely overhauling Apple’s supply chain, manufacturing systems and global distribution.Cook’s procurement and operations background proved to be an ideal match for Apple's recovery and for Jobs' management approach. Speaking to biographer Walter Isaacson for the book Steve Jobs, the late Apple co-founder reflected on their dynamic:“He had the same vision I did. We could interact at a high strategic level, and I could just forget about a lot of things unless he came and pinged me.”Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Donald Trump to Americans protesting against data centres in the US: You are making China very happy
articles.summary: Tech News News: Donald Trump has told Americans campaigning against new data centres that their protests are a gift to Beijing, escalating a fight that has travelled .
articles.body: Donald Trump has told Americans campaigning against new data centres that their protests are a gift to Beijing, escalating a fight that has travelled from small-town council meetings to the centre of the November midterm campaign. In a Truth Social post on Monday, the US president said communities that reject the vast computing warehouses behind the artificial intelligence boom must want to end up "backwards and poor", and called on the country to "let Data Reign".The post went further than his usual pitch about jobs and tax revenue. Trump warned that Americans "will only have yourselves to blame" if the projects are killed off, and said China "could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement". He has been building to this line for weeks. Trump used the same China argument last week in an interview with Michael Cohen, his former fixer, insisting the US led in AI "by a lot". Xi Jinping is due at the White House next month.Opposition to data centres is now bipartisan, and the polling shows itA national survey conducted earlier this month found 61 per cent of Americans opposed a data centre being built in their own community, including 47 per cent of Republicans. On Trump's core claim, that towns without data centres will be left behind, 51 per cent said they disagreed with him.The resistance is already changing outcomes on the ground. The research group Data Center Watch counted at least 75 projects worth roughly $130 billion blocked or delayed by local campaigns in the first three months of 2026 alone. Monterey Park in California, Prince William County in Virginia and Wake County in North Carolina have all fought proposals and won.Electricity bills, not artificial intelligence, are what residents object toThe complaints tend to be practical rather than ideological. Residents point to rising utility bills, groundwater use in drought-hit states, constant low-frequency noise and farmland disappearing under windowless sheds. In New Mexico, an environmental group has challenged well-drilling permits tied to Project Jupiter, a $165 billion Oracle and OpenAI complex planned near the Mexican border. Nationally, Oracle, Meta, Google, Amazon and Microsoft expect to put more than $700 billion into US data centres this year alone.Vice President JD Vance, speaking to reporters at Joint Base Andrews on Monday, put a number on it. Nearly all the backlash, he said, comes from places where a new data centre means a higher power bill for people living next to it. His proposed fix is that operators should be adding electricity to the grid rather than drawing it out.Republicans in tight races are walking away from Trump's positionTexas Governor Greg Abbott spent a year selling data centres before ordering regulators to hold approvals pending audits, and has promised to go after the state's billion-dollar-plus annual tax break for them. New York Governor Kathy Hochul ordered a one-year ban on large projects in July. Michigan Senate nominee Mike Rogers and Stacy Garrity, running for governor in Pennsylvania, have both called for temporary halts.The sharpest test is Ohio, where Sherrod Brown has spent millions on advertising that brands Senator Jon Husted the face of data centres in the state, and where a Republican Senate campaign memo called the issue the anchor around Husted's neck. In Wisconsin, Tom Tiffany is running an ad that renames his Democratic opponent "Data Center David Crowley". Crowley has since said no community should be forced to take a project it does not want.Trump is betting that the argument about beating China outranks the argument about the monthly power bill. November will show whether that bet holds.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Algeria’s president seeks death penalty for those who start forest fires
articles.summary: Abdelmadjid Tebboune’s call comes after wildfires killed at least 12 people and injured 54 in northeastern Algeria.
articles.body:
Algeria's President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has called for the death penalty for anyone who deliberately starts a forest fire after at least 12 people died in wildfires in the country's northeast.

Tebboune ordered Algeria's justice minister on Sunday to submit a proposal by September 15 to amend the penal code to allow capital punishment for those convicted of intentionally setting forest fires, state media reported.

Algeria's penal code already allows the death penalty for several offences, though the country has not carried one out since 1993.

Deliberately starting forest fires currently carries up to 30 years in prison, or life imprisonment in some cases.

Tebboune also ordered provincial governors to hand over all available information about the fires to security authorities, pointing to the possibility that some of the blazes were started deliberately.

"We saw videos and noticed that a number of fires broke out at the same time, at around 1am, which raises many questions," he said.

His call came after Algeria observed three days of national mourning over the deaths of the 12 people in the provinces of Jijel, Bejaia, and Tizi Ouzou. At least 54 others were injured.

The president on Monday ordered authorities to compensate affected families and set up committees to assess losses and determine compensation for damaged property.

He instructed officials to restore electricity, gas, water and telecommunications in affected areas by Saturday at the latest, and told housing authorities to arrange repairs to damaged homes.

Tebboune said normal life should resume in the affected areas within a week.

At least 46 fires are still burning across the country, and a total of 193 fires have been recorded in the past 24 hours.

articles.title: A Guatemalan immigrant began delivering pizzas in Dallas in 1987; decades later she built a franchise training organisation
articles.summary: US News: Aicha Bascaro arrived in the United States as an immigrant from Guatemala and, in 1987, took a job delivering pizzas at a Domino's restaurant in Dalla.
articles.body: Aicha Bascaro arrived in the United States as an immigrant from Guatemala and, in 1987, took a job delivering pizzas at a Domino's restaurant in Dallas, Texas. What began as an entry-level job became the starting point for a career spanning more than three decades and almost every level of the franchise industry. Bascaro worked as a crew member and manager before moving into senior positions, including director of operations, vice president, international consultant and eventually brand president, where she oversaw more than 300 locations across the country. Along the way, she saw a gap that she believed was easy to overlook: franchise owners could be taught how to operate a particular brand without necessarily receiving the broader business education needed to lead and grow a company. That idea eventually became the foundation for the American Franchise Academy. In 2016, a struggling franchisee contacted Bascaro looking for help with a failing business, and instead of simply offering informal advice, she developed a structured training program around the problems he was facing. The American Franchise Academy was founded on July 18, 2016, and a decade later has grown into a specialised organisation focused on business management education for franchisees and their teams.Why Aicha Bascaro says franchisors teach the brand but not the businessAccording to the International Franchise Association, Bascaro created the academy around what she considers one of the franchise industry's biggest gaps. Franchisors generally provide extensive training on their own brands, teaching new owners how their particular systems work and how to operate according to established standards. Bascaro's view is that this brand-specific training does not necessarily cover the wider business skills required to lead and grow a franchise. She has described the distinction simply: franchisors provide the brand and train franchisees to operate it, but they cannot provide the broader business acumen. That, she says, is where the American Franchise Academy comes in, offering training focused on helping franchisees become stronger business leaders rather than simply better operators of a particular brand.The idea came from Bascaro's own experience in the industry. Having progressed from delivering pizzas to senior leadership roles, she had spent years seeing how responsibilities changed as people moved from working inside individual locations to managing larger operations. By the time the struggling franchisee contacted her in 2016, she had accumulated the practical experience to recognise that his problem was not necessarily a lack of effort or knowledge about the brand itself. He needed a more structured understanding of how to manage the business. That first training program eventually became the starting point for an academy built around a much broader idea: franchise ownership requires more than knowing the rules of the brand.How the academy's three programs serve different levels of a franchise organisationThe American Franchise Academy now divides its main curriculum into three programs designed for different levels of responsibility within a franchise organisation.MANAGE provides business-management education for single-unit franchisees and unit managers. The program is aimed at people responsible for the performance of an individual location and focuses on giving them a structured foundation in franchise business management.LEAD is designed for district managers, who oversee multiple locations and therefore operate at a different level from managers responsible for a single unit. The academy offers certification through the program, reflecting the additional responsibilities involved in managing teams and operations across several locations.At the top of the academy's structure is COMMAND, its flagship program. It brings together the broader curriculum intended for franchisees who want to lead and grow their businesses. The three-level structure allows the academy to address people at different stages of the franchise hierarchy rather than treating every operator as though they face the same challenges.Over its first decade, the academy says it has certified more than 400 district managers, more than 200 unit managers and around 100 franchisees. Its participants have come from some of the biggest names in franchising, including McDonald's, Popeyes, Dairy Queen, Subway, Dunkin' and Anytime Fitness. Those numbers also illustrate how the academy has moved beyond the single franchisee whose problems inspired Bascaro to create the original training program. What began as an attempt to help one struggling business has developed into a formal education system serving franchise professionals across multiple major brands.What Bascaro built beyond the academy's formal programsBascaro's work has expanded beyond classroom-style certification. During the academy's first decade, she also built a wider collection of educational material around franchise management, including three Amazon bestselling books and a weekly blog focused on franchising and business education. She also hosts the Franchise Success Formulas podcast, which has attracted more than 19,000 YouTube subscribers. Together, the books, blog, podcast and certification programs have allowed the academy to reach people at different stages of their franchise careers and through different formats.Bascaro has also received recognition within the franchise industry. Her honours include being named to Nation's Restaurant News' 2022 Power List and receiving a Trailblazer Award. She also serves as a Certified Franchise Executive instructor for the International Franchise Association. The broader body of work reflects the same distinction that shaped the academy from the beginning. Bascaro's focus is not simply on teaching franchisees how to follow the operating model of a particular company. Instead, the academy treats business management as a separate area of education that franchise operators can continue developing throughout their careers. That distinction becomes particularly important when a franchisee grows. Running one location and leading a larger franchise operation involve different levels of responsibility, and the academy's programs are structured around those different stages.What comes next for the American Franchise Academy after 10 yearsThe academy is now looking beyond its first decade and toward expanding the reach of its training. One of its priorities is developing multilingual programs that could make the academy's business-management education available to franchise operators around the world rather than primarily serving English-speaking participants. The organisation is also expanding its work directly with franchisors. Through its franchisor partnership strategy, the academy aims to help individual brands provide structured business-management education to their franchise networks through an outside training organisation. Instead of requiring franchisees to find this kind of education independently, the model would allow brands to make it part of the wider support available to their operators.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
